structure_summary.name: 5FQL
structure_summary.scope: Model 1 of the deposited asymmetric unit as parsed; no biological assembly is generated and no coordinates are modified by an audit.

findings.title: CA site A:1551: likely_catalytic, coordination number 6

fields.pdbx_details: 0.1 M MES PH=6.1 1.0 M LICL 20% PEG6K

options.label: Nonbonded 12-6 LJ ion model
trade_offs: Cheapest and fully transferable; ligands may exchange freely.

For divalent ions a single 12-6 parameter set cannot reproduce hydration free energy, ion-oxygen distance and coordination number at once (Li & Merz 2014), so the first shell may rearrange or collapse during sampling.

options.label: Nonbonded 12-6-4 LJ-type ion model
trade_offs: Adds an ion-induced-dipole (1/r^4) term; reproduces hydration free energy, ion-oxygen distance and coordination number for +2 ions (Li & Merz 2014).
Modest overhead; needs C4 terms for each ion/atom-type pair; does not treat charge transfer explicitly.

options.label: Bonded model (MCPB.py-style)
trade_offs: Keeps the crystallographic coordination geometry by construction.

Needs QM calculations for force constants and charges (Li & Merz 2016); ligand exchange is impossible, which biases any landscape where site rearrangement matters; must be rebuilt if a variant changes a ligand.

options.label: Nonbonded ion plus distance restraints to crystal ligands
trade_offs: Cheap way to hold the site together without QM parameterization.
Restraints add a bias to every free energy computed; the restraint set must be recorded and identical across WT and variants to keep comparisons fair.

findings.rationale: A metal site cannot be simulated without choosing an ion model, and the choice changes the site's behaviour. The coordination shell (donor atoms within the cutoff), a geometry descriptor (RMS deviation of L-M-L angles from ideal polyhedra) and the classification are reported as evidence. Classification criteria, in order: the shell contains a non-standard polymer residue or a non-polymer ligand -> likely catalytic; an open site (few protein donors plus water) -> likely catalytic; at least the structural minimum of protein donors -> likely structural; otherwise ambiguous.

references.citation: Harding MM. Small revisions to predicted distances around metal sites in proteins. Acta Crystallogr D Biol Crystallogr. 2006;62(Pt 6):678-682.
Li P, Merz KM Jr. Taking into account the ion-induced dipole interaction in the nonbonded model of ions. J Chem Theory Comput. 2014;10(1):289-297.
Li P, Merz KM Jr. MCPB.py: a Python based metal center parameter builder. J Chem Inf Model. 2016;56(4):599-604.

verify_flags: [VERIFY] 3.0 A shell cutoff: margin above Ca-O target distances (about 2.4 A, with wide scatter) in Harding 2006; not re-read from the full text in this session.
[VERIFY] structural_min_protein_donors = 5 is a working heuristic, not a literature value; no open-site criterion is applied to Ca.

findings.title: Formylglycine (sulfatase catalytic residue): ALS A:84

evidence.value: C CA CB N O OG OS1 OS2 OS3 OS4 S

evidence.note: from the atoms present in the deposited residue

options.label: Model FGly as the aldehyde hydrate (gem-diol, FGH)
trade_offs: The species proposed to perform the nucleophilic attack in the transesterification-elimination mechanism (Demydchuk et al. 2017).
Needs a parameterized non-standard residue; replaces the deposited sulfate ester, so the covalent sulfate is removed (record that decision too).

options.label: Model FGly as the free aldehyde
trade_offs: The form produced by FGE and regenerated after sulfate elimination.
Not the catalytically active hydrate; needs its own parameters.

options.label: Keep the deposited FGly sulfate ester (covalent intermediate)
trade_offs: Matches the deposited coordinates and the Ca2+ coordination by sulfate oxygens.
Simulates an intermediate, not the resting enzyme; the authors note the density could alternatively be a phosphate ester.

options.label: Revert to cysteine (the unmodified precursor)
trade_offs: Standard parameters.
Removes the catalytic chemistry; only defensible for questions that do not involve the active site.

findings.rationale: Eukaryotic sulfatases carry C-alpha-formylglycine, post-translationally formed from a cysteine, as the catalytic residue. Its hydration / esterification state (free aldehyde, gem-diol hydrate, or sulfate/phosphate ester intermediate) changes the active site's chemistry and the metal coordination, so it is an explicit decision and never a silent default.

references.citation: Demydchuk M, Hill CH, Zhou A, et al. Insights into Hunter syndrome from the structure of iduronate-2-sulfatase. Nat Commun. 2017;8:15786.
Dierks T, Schmidt B, Borissenko LV, et al. Multiple sulfatase deficiency is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the human C(alpha)-formylglycine generating enzyme. Cell. 2003;113(4):435-444.

verify_flags: [VERIFY] DDZ is taken from Demydchuk et al. 2017 ('Protein Data Bank code DDZ: 3,3-dihydroxy-alanine'); not checked against the wwPDB Chemical Component Dictionary in this session. ALS was checked only against the 5FQL file's own chem_comp record.

[VERIFY] Treating ALS as formylglycine sulfate ester is a chemical identification ((3S)-3-(sulfooxy)-L-serine = C-alpha-formylglycine hydrate monosulfate); ALS in another entry could be a genuine sulfated serine, so check the context when another structure matches.
[VERIFY] No component ID for free formylglycine aldehyde is included; add one only after checking the CCD.

[VERIFY] Recommending the gem-diol follows the paper's statement that FGly acts catalytically as the aldehyde hydrate; whether that is the right state for a given free-energy question is a study decision.

findings.title: Alternative locations with large spread: ARG A:294 (6.19 A)

options.label: Keep the highest-occupancy altloc
trade_offs: Simple and reproducible; ties are broken by altloc identifier (A before B).
Discards the minor state, which may be the functionally relevant one.

options.label: Keep a specific altloc (named in the decision)
trade_offs: Lets the human choose the state relevant to the question.
Mixing altloc letters across residues can create clashes when the letters were not refined as a consistent set; check neighbours.

options.label: Keep each altloc as a separate system (ensemble)
trade_offs: Samples both deposited states; the difference becomes part of the result.
Multiplies the number of systems to prepare and simulate.

findings.rationale: Altlocs that move atoms by 1 A or more are distinct conformations; which one is simulated can change the outcome near a region of interest.

findings.title: Unobserved N-terminal residues: A:26-33 (8 residues)

options.label: Cap the first/last observed residue (neutral ACE/NME-style caps)
trade_offs: Avoids an artificial charged terminus where the real chain continues.
The missing tail's interactions are absent.

options.label: Truncate at the observed residue with a charged terminus
trade_offs: Simplest; standard termini parameters.
Introduces a charge the real protein does not have at that position.

options.label: Model the missing tail
trade_offs: Restores the full sequence.
Modelled tails are unconstrained by density and may dominate conformational sampling if they are long and disordered.

findings.rationale: Unobserved N-terminal residues (often tags, signal peptides or disordered tails).

findings.title: Internal gap (unobserved residues between observed ones): A:444-453 (10 residues)

options.label: Model the missing loop
trade_offs: Restores chain connectivity.
The modelled loop is a hypothesis; its conformation is unconstrained by density and may bias sampling nearby.

options.label: Leave the gap as a chain break, capping both sides
trade_offs: No invented coordinates.
Two artificial termini; the flanking segments can drift apart.

findings.rationale: An internal gap leaves two artificial chain ends. Evidence gives the gap length and the flanking CA-CA distance, compared with the maximum span of the missing residues (3.8 A per peptide unit, the approximate trans CA-CA distance).
verify_flags: [VERIFY] 3.8 A CA-CA distance per residue is the textbook trans-peptide value; no citation attached in this session.

options.label: Expert decision required
trade_offs: Nothing proceeds until a human decides how to treat the chemistry.

trade_offs: Makes the treatment reusable and documented.
Requires a rule with sources and a panel structure that exercises it.

options.label: Exclude from the system (recorded decision)
trade_offs: Removes the unknown chemistry.
Anything it contributes (contacts, charge, covalent attachment) is lost.

options.label: Keep and parameterize outside the rule system
trade_offs: Keeps the deposited chemistry.
The treatment is not captured by a rule, so it must be fully described in the decision rationale.

findings.rationale: Residues that no rule claims: ligands, glycans, ions without a rule, and polymer residues outside the standard set that no non-standard rule matched. Residues joined by annotated covalent connections are reported as one group, together with their attachment to the polymer.
